svg.title: V3 replicated matmul: Operand multicast on each 13×10 worker grid
svg.text: V3 replicated matmul: Operand multicast on each 13×10 worker grid
This grid repeats on all four devices after activation gathering. Transpose maps 13 M workers to x and 10 N workers to y.
Each source reads its A block from gathered DRAM.
Highlighted pipe: (2,0) sends to nine receivers.
One hardware NoC multicast per operand block, not sequential forwarding.
x: M-worker coordinate (0…12); y: N-worker coordinate (0…9)
Each source reads its B block from replicated DRAM.
Highlighted pipe: (0,3) sends to twelve receivers.
One hardware NoC multicast per operand block, not sequential forwarding.
x: M-worker coordinate (0…12); y: N-worker coordinate (0…9)
Every worker combines its activation and weight blocks in L1, initializes the accumulator from bias, performs matmul and writes its assigned output blocks to DRAM.
Blue filled nodes read operands from DRAM; other nodes receive into L1 DFBs. Lines show multicast membership, not chains of intermediate copies.
The two diagrams show the same 130-worker grid. Activation and weight transfers run on separate data-movement kernels while compute executes.
Source: examples/all_gather_minimal_matmul/replicated/operation.py · activation_rows and weight_columns · worker-grid coordinates, not virtual NoC addresses
